title: A/B framework for automated batching & KV-cache configs with dashboarded safety gates
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Build and run a statistically-sound A/B experimentation harness that automatically recommends and safely applies batching and KV-cache configuration changes. The experiment must produce dashboarded metrics, automated rollback signals, and a publishable analysis notebook that quantifies cost savings vs latency/quality trade-offs.
goal: Reduce per-token inference cost by at least 12% on targeted traffic slices while maintaining P95 latency SLO and no measurable degradation on evaluation prompts.
hypothesis: A targeted set of batching + KV-cache configurations (smaller batch size thresholds for short requests + aggressive prefix cache TTL for repeat sessions) will decrease GPU token cost without increasing P95 latency beyond the SLO for 90% of traffic and without increasing model hallucination rates on the eval suite.
experiment_design: Create A (control) = current production batching/caching config. B (variant) = new auto-config generated by recommendation engine. Traffic split 60/40 for three weeks; stratify by route, sequence-length bucket, and customer tier. Use feature gating to limit variant to non-Sensitive customers. Tie experiment to rollouts with canary ramps at 5/20/40/60/100% for variant after statistical checks pass.
metrics: Primary: cost_per_1k_tokens (USD), P95_latency_ms, request_error_rate. Secondary: P50_latency_ms, tail_99_latency_ms, model_quality_regression_percent on evaluation prompt set, throughput (tokens/sec). Statistical metrics: lift %, Cohen's d, 95% CI, p-value (two-sided).
guardrails: Auto-fail experiment and trigger rollback if: (1) P95_latency_ms increases by >10% vs control for two consecutive days; (2) request_error_rate increases by >0.2 percentage points; (3) model_quality_regression_percent > 1% absolute on eval set. All guardrails must surface in dashboard and send Slack + PagerDuty alert when breached.
sampling_criteria: Only include requests from API routes tagged 'app-text' and 'chat-lite'. Exclude authenticated customers labeled 'regulated' and routes with sequence_length > 4096. Minimum sample size per cohort: 50k requests/day over 3 days to consider statistical power adequate.
rollout_strategy: Phase 0: dry-run in staging with synthetic load. Phase 1: 5% canary on production weekdays with dedicated dashboards. Phase 2: automated ramp if daily statistical tests pass and guardrails not violated. Phase 3: promote to full traffic and publish analysis notebook and Grafana dashboard links.
monitoring_dashboards: New Grafana dashboard 'batch-cache-ab/ENG-23678' with panels: cost per 1k tokens (by route), P95/P50/99 latency by variant, error rate by variant, eval-quality time series, cohort-level sessions with cache hit ratio, kernel utilization (GPU%), and experiment health summary card. Panels include PromQL queries and links to underlying logs.
analysis_notebooks: Jupyter notebook (analysis/ENG-23678-ab-analysis.ipynb) with sections: data ingest SQL, pre-processing, exploratory plots, statistical tests (bootstrap and t-test), uplift tables by bucket, and final recommendation. Notebook will be in /repos/notebooks/cost-opt.
success_criteria: Cost_per_1k_tokens: >=12% reduction at 95% CI without violating any guardrail. No degradation >0.5% on eval-quality for critical prompt set. Operational: dashboards live and automated rollback path validated in staging.
rollback_plan: Automated rollback job bound to experiment id: if guardrail breached, rollout controller instantaneously swaps routing policy back to control for affected traffic slices and triggers a read-only incident in SRE runbook. Post-mortem: within 48 hours with root cause and config tuning. Playbook link included in links.
timeline: Week 1: implement variant config generator and feature flag. Week 2: build dashboards + notebook + staging dry-run. Week 3: canary + analysis. Week 4: full rollout and publish results.
notes: Variant config uses new 'adaptive-batch-threshold' heuristic from research branch.
Work coordinates with Runtime Kernel Team for kernel selection telemetry to attribute cost changes.
We must ensure sampling doesn't bias toward low-latency customers — stratify by customer_tier.
Estimate assumes synthetic traffic load availability from perf infra team for staging validation.
